svg.title: FoveaWAM conceptual architecture
svg.desc: FoveaWAM architecture with aligned input-token rows and the accepted compact v2 layer, rotated counterclockwise by 90 degrees. Stream positions are reordered to Scene, Summary, Action from top to bottom, preserving shared attention and both residual stages. RGB is a Blender illustration of the recorded state; depth remains from the original recording. Current RGB-D, target history, robot state and noisy actions occupy four equally spaced input rows. Larger token glyphs form one packed column: visual, target and robot segments form S, learned summaries form M, and noisy actions form A. Color and small gaps separate segments; no collector or external ingress arrows are drawn. Only the visual frontend is shown as a Vision Encoder, contracting toward tokens. Scene and Summary share one World FFN; Action uses its own FFN. Panel labels and whitespace group the unframed overview and two lower details. The block attention mask identifies query and key directions, uses S/M/A role colors, and hatches its blocked cells. M uses a related cool color while the shared World FFN retains one world color. Final patch and pooled-summary states support geometric readouts; dashed arrows denote training-only readouts, as explained in the caption. Actions are generated from hidden states, not decoded geometry. A compact joint-training row branches only to World supervision and Action flow matching. Inference first prepares S/M once and stores their per-layer attention-input K/V. This fixed bank conditions the Action branch from above. A separate horizontal path carries Gaussian noise through repeated Action updates to one robot action-chunk icon; its feedback loop does not include world prefill or the cache. Target history uses miniature SE(3) glyphs from recorded past states in one shared reference frame and display scale, retaining cumulative motion against the same pale historical reference. Robot symbols are original editable vectors with no image background. Geometric examples are recorded supervision labels and token glyph multiplicity is schematic.
